output:
To: kitbash-market/murmur-dialogue/reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: 4 stars - my whole game is built on this, but use 3.1.4 for now

I've used Murmur since August 2022, when I paid 19 dollars for v1.3. That weekend I built the first prototype of Lanternfolk with it, the ferryman scene, and it worked well enough that I quit my job at a mobile studio a few weeks later. Four years on, Lanternfolk has 412 dialogue nodes and ships in 9 languages through Murmur's CSV export. So I'm biased, but I've also used it longer and harder than most people here.

I'm giving it 4 stars. It would be 5 if 3.2 wasn't broken and if there was still support. If you're thinking about buying it now, here is the honest version.

**What's broken in 3.2.0**

If you load a save that was made in 3.1.x, every Murmur variable resets to its default. In our game that means the ferryman forgets you already paid him, and every other flag goes the same way. My guess is that the save key changed from node path to uid between versions, but I haven't dug into it properly. Several of us in the forum have hit the same bug.

**How to fix it (roll back to 3.1.4)**

1. Get the 3.1.4 release.
2. In your project, replace the Murmur folder in `addons` with the 3.1.4 one.
3. Keep a copy of 3.1.4 somewhere safe and don't update to 3.2.

After that our old saves loaded fine again. tobbe_codes in the forum confirmed it works for them too. One caveat: I haven't tested saves that were *created* in 3.2 and then loaded back in 3.1.4, so back up your project and saves before you switch. If you're starting a new project, I'd just start on 3.1.4.

**What's not coming**

Ines has said 3.2 is the last version she'll make. Don't buy it expecting bug fixes or answers to support questions. You're buying it as it is.

**What you still get**

3.1.4 is solid. Branching, conditions, variables, barks, voice line hooks and the localisation export all work, and I'm shipping a commercial game on it next month. It's still the nicest dialogue tool for Godot that I've used, and I've tried a few. The source is also on the public repo under MIT now, so you aren't locked in. If something breaks you can fix it yourself, and anyone can fork it. I might look at a fork myself after we launch, but I'm not promising anything, so don't count on me.

**About some of the other reviews**

I get being angry when an update breaks your saves. I was annoyed too. But "took our money and ran" isn't fair. Ines shipped four years of updates on a tool I paid 19 dollars for, she told everyone plainly that she was stepping back, and she opened up the source so the community can carry it on. That isn't running. Plenty of plugins just disappear without a word. People step away from projects for all kinds of reasons, and she doesn't owe anyone an explanation.

**Should you buy it?**

If you're fine staying on 3.1.4 and you're comfortable owning the code from here on, yes, it's still worth it. If you need a tool with active support and future Godot updates guaranteed, wait and see if a fork appears, or look elsewhere.

Ines, if you ever read this: thank you. Lanternfolk wouldn't exist without Murmur, and that's not an exaggeration. I hope you get to play it someday.

- Jonna, Stugaspel
